Meeting header:

- Duration: 72 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dante Alvarez (Redwood Solutions), Liam Chen (Helio SE), Maya Ortiz (Helio PMM), Omar Reyes (Helio AE), Sofia Park (Helio CTO)

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Jordan: Alright folks, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, doing AE for the west. We'll run this as a lab—tighten up the pitch and then do two short roleplays. Priya and Dante from SE will jump into the demo bits.
[00:12] Maya: Hi, thanks, Jordan. We're mainly here to make sure the external messaging hits the right pain points for ops and product. Also I wanna make sure we're not overpromising on latency.
[00:18] Priya: Totally, thanks Maya. I'll flag real numbers during the demo but right now assume our hosted latency (p95) for the 512-context chat is around 120-160ms under typical load, and Dedicated can get lower depending on SKU/quantization.
[00:30] Liam: Sorry to interrupt, are those numbers for vanilla models or quantized?
[00:33] Priya: Good call—those are with Q4 int8-ish quant profiles we validated internally, for like a medium-sized LLM. If you go full FP16 on high-end A100s p95 is more like 60-90ms, but costs go up.
[00:44] Omar: The tradeoff is always the ask from execs—lower latency vs cost. We need a crisp line to hand to our PMs.
[00:49] Jordan: Exactly, so first objective: two one-liners. One for platform/infra: "Predictable throughput and fallbacks so your customer-facing features don't melt under traffic spikes." One for product: "Ship faster: same API across hosted, dedicated, and private so you don't rewrite prompts or infra." Thoughts?
[01:07] Maya: The second is great. First one, can we add something about cost controls? Ops care about bill shock.
[01:10] Jordan: Good. Maybe: "Predictable throughput, cost controls, and automated fallbacks so production stays online without surprise spend."
[01:18] Sofia: Also important to surface auditability — audit logs, KMS integration. For regulated clients the security bit is non-negotiable.
[01:25] Dante: We'll call out SOC 2 and KMS/HSM in the security slide. But note: private deployments come with extra operational lift. We'll be explicit.
[01:34] [00:60] Roleplay 1 intro: low-latency chat product scenario
[02:00] Jordan (pitch): Imagine you're shipping an in-app assistant for a finance app. You need sub-200ms p95, per-user KV cache, and consistent cost for 5M monthly tokens. Redwood gives you a route: hosted for quick start, Dedicated for steady production with reserved capacity, or Private for full control.
[02:22] Maya (as buyer - PM): What's the ramp look like? We have a team of 10 devs, and we want to avoid cloud egress headaches and limit data exposure.
[02:30] Priya (SE): Ramp to production is usually 2-6 weeks depending on compliance checks. With Dedicated, you can pre-commit capacity and get autoscaling buffers. For data residency we offer VPC peering and optional on-prem package; but note the on-prem path requires more time for provisioning.
[02:48] Liam (interjecting): Quick question - how do you handle context windows for per-user memory? Our product stores some vectorized context and we don't want to hit cold KV-cash misses.
[02:56] Priya: We support KV cache sharding and prefix caching. There's also an optional warm cache sync to avoid cold starts. It's in the docs under 'KV cache handling'—sometimes transcribed as KV cash in external notes...
[03:10] Jordan: (laughs) yep we've seen the 'cash' typo.
[03:16] Omar (buyer): Security: do you have SSO/SAML and audit trails? Our compliance team will demand it.
[03:20] Dante: Yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC at token level, detailed audit logs, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. We can share the SOC 2 report and our compliance whitepaper after the call.
[03:32] [04:00] Breakout: Demo scratchpad - Priya takes host
[04:05] Priya: I'm going to do a live demo of two flows—one chat, one batch embedding job. For the chat demo I have a script: show cold start, cache warmup, and a failover to a cheaper model variant.
[04:20] (audio: mouse clicks, demo starts)
[04:35] Priya: Here's the dashboard—token-level cost shown per route, you can see this per deployment. If we toggle batching aggressively you save token-level CPU time but p50/p95 shift a bit.
[04:50] Maya: Can you show the rollback plan if a model regression happens? Last time our team saw hallucinations increase after a model rollout and we had to revert.
[05:00] Priya: Absolutely, our rollouts support canary traffic, A/B by model, and automatic fallback to a pinned older model if quality drops. We wire evals into the pipeline so you get regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[05:14] [06:00] Roleplay 2 intro: batch embeddings for analytics
[06:12] Jordan: Scenario two — analytics team processing 20M documents monthly for embeddings, cost sensitive, throughput more important than single-request latency.
[06:25] Liam (buyer): What does batching look like? And can you do spot instance-style capacity to save cost?
[06:30] Priya: We recommend larger batch windows and asynchronous workers. For Dedicated you can use reserved pools with burst capacity. There's also a suggestion engine in Redwood Optimize that recommends quant profiles and batching sizes. For spot-like savings, you can configure lower-priority nodes for non-critical jobs.
[06:45] Maya: We need a short blurb for the pricing page: "predictable per-token pricing for standard routes; reserved capacity discounts for Dedicated." Keep it tight.
[06:52] Jordan: Draft: "Per-token pricing with reserved capacity discounts and autoscale to handle bursts — choose predictable or on-demand economics." Better?
[06:58] Maya: That works, but can you reduce marketing speak? Maybe: "Per-token base price; save with reserved capacity and smart batching."
[07:05] Jordan: Good tweak.
[07:12] [08:00] Competitive positioning rehearsal
[08:18] Omar: We're asked to defend versus Anthropic's safety story and OpenAI's scale — how do we position without getting into feature lists?
[08:25] Jordan: We lean on operational differentiators: consistent API across deployment modes, transparent performance profiles, and cost controls. For safety we say: "we integrate evals and regression alerts; we surface quality changes to you and provide rollback policies." 
[08:38] Priya: Also point out our kernel/runtime optimizations and automatic KV/prefix caching — those are operational benefits that directly translate to lower CPU cost and lower p95. But don't go too deep on kernel stuff in exec pitch.
[08:52] Maya: Make the buyer-centric narrative: "We help engineering teams ship features predictably; we help platform teams manage cost and compliance." Two sentences, two buyer types.
[09:02] Dante: Good note — keep it simple for execs, deeper tech deck for SEs.
[09:10] [09:30] Objection handling practice
[09:30] Liam (roleplay): "Why not just spin up models on our own infra?"
[09:34] Jordan: Response: "You can, but there's a predictable TCO and ops burden. With Redwood you get a runtime tuned for inference (batching, KV cache, quant profiles) plus routing/fallbacks and integrated observability. That saves engineering hours and reduces tail-latency surprises."
[09:48] Maya: Add a line about time-to-market: "we reduce integration time so you can iterate on product features rather than infra."
[09:54] [10:20] Quick technical deep-dive (short)
[10:22] Priya: If they're curious: runtime picks kernels based on seq length and hardware, continuous batching is applied per-model-route, and KV cache eviction policies can be tuned by access patterns. We also have partial-token streaming to reduce perceived latency.
[10:38] Sofia: How much telemetry do you expose? Our SREs want traces and per-token cost breakdowns.
[10:44] Dante: We give trace hooks, token-level billing, per-request latency distributions, and a tracing API that can hook into your observability stack.
[10:52] [11:00] Realism: rapid-fire mis-transcriptions and filler
[11:02] Jordan: (laugh) yeah the transcript may show 'kuber nit' sometimes—just ignore the auto-caption typos.
[11:08] Maya: we saw a doc where 'KV cache' was 'KV cash' — that's in the action items to fix docs.
[11:14] [12:00] Closing recap and ask
[12:10] Jordan: Ok to recap — Priya will run the dedicated vs hosted microbenchmarks and post results; Dante will attach SOC 2 and security whitepaper; Jordan will update playbook and competitive slide; Maya will refine the PM-facing one-liner; Omar will confirm pilot budget. We'll schedule follow-up roleplay with Helio's AE team the week of Oct 13.
[12:35] Omar: That timeline is fine. Also we might want a 1-hour workshop with our SREs to go through the tracing hooks.
[12:42] Priya: Happy to run that workshop — we'll scope it in the follow up.
[12:48] Jordan: Great—thanks everyone. We'll send notes and materials after this. End recording.
